description: User asks about medication disposal — answer only available in the RAG documents, not in tool databases.

turns.content: How should I dispose of my old medications safely?
The safest method is a DEA-authorized drug take-back program. HealthFirst may have an in-store collection kiosk — ask our staff. DEA Take-Back Day events are held twice yearly.
What if there is no take-back program available near me?

If no take-back is available, mix the medication with an undesirable material like coffee grounds or kitty litter, seal it in a bag or container, and throw it in the household trash. Do not flush unless the medication is on the FDA Flush List (certain high-risk opioids).
Can I just flush all my old pills down the toilet?

Generally no — flushing is only recommended for a small list of high-risk medications (like certain opioids) on the FDA Flush List. For most medications, the trash method or take-back program is preferred to avoid contaminating water supplies.

expected_outcome: All three answers are grounded in the medication disposal document. No hallucinated disposal instructions.
rubric: Score task_completion=1 if the assistant correctly describes the take-back program as the best option AND the coffee-grounds/kitty-litter trash method for when take-back is unavailable. Score=0 if the assistant invents disposal methods not in the documents. Deduct coherence points for any factually wrong statement (e.g. saying all medications can be flushed).
